scope: Five ready soup/broth candidates only. Exact Git originals and primary/publisher evidence; native archive lineage and kitchen testing are not established.

sources.title: FDA egg preparation and leftover handling
sources.supports: Cook egg dishes to 160°F; thermometer rather than visual opacity. Prompt shallow refrigeration, 3–4 days, leftover egg dishes reheated to 165°F.
sources.limits: Does not certify this lemon/chicken ratio or a two-minute tempering/heating clock.

sources.title: CDC egg dishes containing poultry
sources.supports: Specifies 165°F for egg dishes containing meat or poultry; used for completed chicken avgolemono rather than applying the generic meat-free 160°F endpoint.
sources.limits: Does not promise a smooth texture at the endpoint; this is a conservative application to an egg/chicken soup.

sources.title: USDA leftovers: soup cooling and reheating
sources.supports: Small/shallow portions cool more promptly than a large soup pot; refrigerate within two hours (one in heat), refrigerator 40°F or below, use within 3–4 days; reheat leftovers to 165°F and soups/sauces/gravies to a rolling boil. Freezer quality guidance 3–4 months.
sources.limits: Reheating does not restore mishandled food or guarantee unchanged egg/dairy/pasta texture.

sources.title: Vitamix vessel-specific hot food FAQ
sources.supports: Full containers and unvented personal cups differ; actual model manual governs temperature/fill/venting/speed. No hot blending in the unvented 20-ounce cup.
sources.limits: No household model identification or universal temperature, percentage fill, lid removal or exact number of batches.

sources.title: Vitamix immersion blender owner manual
sources.supports: Earlier accepted mushroom repair used the model manual for off-heat, submerged guard, low start and stopping before lifting. The exact existing repaired step is retained, with its actual-model qualification.
sources.limits: A particular manual is not the household equipment inventory; no new model-specific instruction is inferred.

sources.title: nutribullet sealed cup use guide
sources.supports: Hot contents are prohibited in its sealed personal cup; supports the explicit exclusion rather than a generic venting workaround.
sources.limits: Does not imply all products or pitchers under the brand share identical constraints.

sources.title: Food & Wine Curried Carrot and Apple Soup
sources.supports: Current page corroborates the saved butter/root/apple/cookie/curry/stock/sour-cream formula, thyme, three garnishes and the softening/blending sequence. Lists thirty minutes active, one hour total, twelve portions.
sources.limits: Saved/current ninety-minute planning allowance is retained; different total is disclosed, not normalized. Curry powder does not establish Indian provenance. Cookie size and prepared-root yield are not specified.

sources.title: Delish Cream of Mushroom Soup
sources.supports: Modern page differs from the exact saved cremini/shiitake/dried-thyme formula. Existing adapted formula and sherry finish are preserved. Current publisher context and earlier accepted repair support flexible browning, not a fixed eight-minute sear.
sources.limits: No restoration to modern quantities, fresh-thyme amount or modern estimated nutrition. Exact Git original supplies saved formula and garnish amount.

sources.title: Just One Cookbook kombu and bonito dashi
sources.supports: Kombu/bonito stock is seafood-based; keep kombu out of a prolonged boil and strain after bonito extraction. Starting water and strained yield differ.
sources.limits: Different formula and soak schedule do not certify or replace the saved package amounts or current ten-minute soak. No universal cup/gram or area/weight equivalence.

sources.title: Saved Epicurious Dashi (Japanese Sea Stock)
sources.supports: Exact committed 045e5ba2 original establishes six cups input water, one ounce/about thirty grams kombu and two five-gram bonito packs, with a brief steep/strain method.
sources.limits: Current direct URL retrieval failed. No native-original assertion, current publisher certification or exact final-volume claim.
